full_judgment:
37. On perusal of evidence on record it appears that the defendant No.1 filed the original copy of registered Deed Nos.8567 and 5078 dated 28-6-1967 and 15-9-1966 which were marked as Exhibits A and A-1 respectively. Exhibits A and A-1 were executed by the heirs of Monu Meah and the deeds are thirty years old original documents submitted before the court from the proper custody and, as such, those deeds carries a presumption of correctness as per provision of section 90 of the Evidence Act. Moreover, the plaintiff of the instant suit as well as the executants of those deeds i.e. the heirs of the Monu Meah did not challenge the same as such the deeds which were marked as Exhibits A and A-1 stands as proper and genuine. 

 "90. Presumption as to documents thirty years old: Where any document, purporting or proved to be thirty years old, is produced from any custody which the court in the particular case considers proper, the Court may presume that the signature and every other part of such document, which purports to be in the handwriting of any particular person, is in that person's handwriting, and, in the case of a document executed or attested, that it was duly executed and attested by the person by whom it purports to be executed and attested." 

 45. But the trial court misconstrued the provisions of the Evidence Act inasmuch as the documents which were marked as Exhibits A, A-1 and A-2 carries a presumption of their correctness as per provision of section 90 of the Evidence Act which is discussed earlier. In this context the person who denied the correctness of those deeds, burden of disproving the same is lies upon him/her according to the provisions of the Evidence Act. Though the plaintiff denied the same but they did not take any step to disprove those deeds.
